events.title: Coronation of Queen Elizabeth II
events.description: Elizabeth II was crowned at Westminster Abbey in London, in a ceremony that was the first British coronation to be fully televised. The event was watched by millions around the world and followed her accession to the throne in February 1952.
events.significance: Marked the formal start of a reign that became the longest in British history and helped popularize television as a mass medium for global events.

events.title: Indian Citizenship Act Signed
events.description: President Calvin Coolidge signed the Indian Citizenship Act, granting U.S. citizenship to all Native Americans born within the territorial limits of the United States.
events.significance: Extended citizenship to Native Americans, although many states continued to restrict their voting rights for decades afterward.

events.title: Surveyor 1 Lands on the Moon
events.description: NASA's Surveyor 1 spacecraft made the first soft landing by a U.S. spacecraft on the Moon, in the Oceanus Procellarum, and transmitted thousands of photographs back to Earth.
events.significance: Demonstrated the feasibility of soft lunar landings and provided data on the lunar surface that supported planning for the Apollo missions.

events.title: Italy Votes to Abolish the Monarchy
events.description: In a national referendum, Italians voted to become a republic rather than retain the House of Savoy, with women voting in a national election for the first time. King Umberto II subsequently left the country.
events.significance: Established the Italian Republic, which is celebrated annually as Republic Day, and shaped the postwar political order of Italy.

events.title: Birth of Thomas Hardy
events.description: English novelist and poet Thomas Hardy was born in Dorset, England. He later wrote works such as Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Far from the Madding Crowd, and Jude the Obscure.
events.significance: Hardy became one of the leading figures of English literature, bridging Victorian realism and modernist poetry.
